samples.marker_line: Kothamine agent: hidden relay and DLL injection; add coverage
samples.identification: Self-described Kothamine Windows agent prototype (C++ source, sniffed as C).
execution_trace: main creates a named mutex and returns on ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS; this is a short-lived launcher guard, not persistence.
main expands a roaming-AppData Microsoft updater DLL path and invokes inject_into_explorer(0, dll). PID 0 makes this invocation fail at OpenProcess; Explorer lookup is a placeholder.

The injection routine itself opens a supplied PID, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves kernel32 LoadLibraryA, and passes that pointer plus the remote buffer to CreateRemoteThread. No runtime success is claimed.

main invokes a peer-forwarding helper with a fixed tc-prefixed peer token. The helper expands an AppData tailcat.exe path, builds a forward command mapping 18080:4444, and passes CREATE_NO_WINDOW plus SW_HIDE startup configuration to CreateProcessA.
load_feature loads an existing DLL, resolves GetFeatureApi, calls the getter and stores the returned API pointer. It is never called from main; init/exec/cleanup are not invoked in this specimen.

Receiving a Base64 DLL, writing a temporary plugin, extracting a bundled tunnel, talking to a loopback listener, and implementing remote task dispatch are only described in comments or absent. No decoding, persistence, credential theft, or privilege-escalation operation is implemented.
samples.judgment_reason: The updater disguise under roaming AppData, remote DLL injection design, hidden operator-peer relay launch, and explicit defender-evasion commentary make this likely malicious implant source. A source sketch can be a malicious artifact even though its shown PID is invalid and its payload/tunnel binaries are missing. No authorized research or deployment context was supplied.

covered: Hidden peer-forwarding setup in the admitted injector
coverage_goal.why_not_three: Only two distinct hostile outcomes are implemented. Investigated plugin loading, staging/decoding, C2 dispatch, persistence and escalation. Plugin receive/drop/dispatch is absent or comment-only, local plugin loading is dual-use, and there is no persistence/escalation implementation. Additional hostile traits would duplicate evidence or invent behavior.
coverage_goal.matcher_limitation: No missing matcher prevents coverage of an implemented hostile behavior; C/C++ out-parameter/interprocedural flow and runtime success remain limited.

samples.marker_line: Solana Web3 1.78.7: normal SDK outside affected range; fix traits
execution_trace: Keypair.fromSecretKey validates and constructs a local keypair. fromSeed and randomPrivateKey construct local Ed25519 keys. ed25519.sign consumes the private scalar locally.

Ed25519Program.createInstructionWithPrivateKey derives the public key and signature, then constructs an instruction containing public key, signature and message; it does not serialize the private scalar into that instruction.

Connection signs caller-supplied transactions locally, serializes the signed wire transaction, Base64-encodes it, and submits sendTransaction JSON-RPC to the caller-selected endpoint. Fetch middleware and socket reconnection are normal SDK extension and transport behavior.

Executable URL literals identify only official Solana cluster RPC hosts; GitHub URLs in bundled crypto code are documentation. No unrelated key-exfiltration destination or queue path appears in source or distributed variants.

The browser IIFE embeds normal BN, Base58/buffer and cryptographic implementations. Minification and source-map escape layers do not constitute a payload loader. All 357 resolvable source-map source entries equal the supplied TypeScript sources.
samples.judgment_reason: The exact registry artifact implements its documented SDK purpose. Its key handling and network operations form normal transaction signing/submission, without an unrelated secret export path. This version is outside the advisory range; version exclusion corroborates code analysis rather than replacing it.
samples.source_label_explanation: MAL-2024-11183 affects 1.95.6 and 1.95.7, fixed in 1.95.8. OSV also retains an earlier imported introduced=0 origin. The 1.78.7 label is an out-of-range/stale package association; the exact collector error cannot be established.
samples.intent_and_missing_context: Applications can misuse a wallet SDK, and no deployed application or installed dependency lock was supplied. That does not make the unchanged SDK archive malware.

samples.marker_line: TanStack router 1.58.12: normal route compiler; add AST traits
execution_trace: Vite/Rspack/Webpack entry points register unplugin route-generation and route-splitting hooks.
Configuration comes from the project root through @tanstack/router-generator and a Zod schema. Build and file-watch hooks regenerate route files when project routes change.

Babel parses route source to an AST, traverses createRoute/createFileRoute options, replaces component/loader references with lazy imports, removes unused imports/exports through dead-code elimination, and generates JavaScript plus source maps.

The router-generator dependency reads project route sources and tsr.config.json and writes generated route-tree/source files. The virtual-file-routes dependency constructs route descriptions. The dead-code-elimination dependency removes unused AST bindings.

Debug environment reads only control logging. Production process.exit(0) runs after build completion. No install lifecycle script, credential read, unrelated remote fetch, or dynamic evaluation of downloaded code exists.
All 20 resolvable router source-map source entries equal the shipped TypeScript sources; source, ESM and CommonJS behavior are consistent.
samples.judgment_reason: Byte-identical registry code performs the advertised project-local build transformations. Direct dependencies and the source/compiled variants support that explanation; no payload or secret transfer was found.
samples.source_label_explanation: No feed/advisory details were supplied for this file. Possible explanations include confusing legitimate build-code rewriting or the name babel-dead-code-elimination with evasion, or an overbroad package/dependency association. None can be attributed to the external source with certainty.
samples.intent_and_missing_context: A malicious project plugin or later dependency resolution is outside this archive. No deployed project, lockfile, or evidence of such substitution was supplied.

checks.existing_controls_comparison: No finding loss after canonical ID mapping on the Solana WASM attack fixture, obfuscated wallet RPC fixture, BN stub near miss, actual backtick shell fixture, image-launch and desktop-opener controls.
checks.final_gate: make validate (run last; outcome reported in final response)
checks.header_guard: The document profile rejects any #! interpreter-directive prefix, including uncommon shell names. This is a baseline format property; no extra execution or language-identity claim is emitted.

dependencies.selection: Exact lower-bound versions named by the two manifests, including four @types declarations. Original archives and .forage.json provenance are retained in scratch.
dependencies.version_limit: Caret/tilde ranges have no shipped lockfile, so these are inspected permitted releases rather than a reconstruction of a particular deployed dependency tree.
dependencies.analysis: Scanned original dependency archives and registry records, inspected networking/crypto entry paths, Babel/unplugin transformations, TanStack generator/configuration, and bigint-buffer native rebuild. No hostile/suspicious dependency finding appeared, and traced behavior fit library purpose. bigint-buffer installs through node-gyp rebuild with an ordinary JS fallback, not a custom remote payload.

corrections: Retained all existing accurate sample behavior detections; relocated neutral launch, thread-context, key-import, SDK, BN and RPC/schema observations to homes describing their evidence. Consumers and relevant ancestor exclusions were updated.

Removed the misleading Solana credential-access umbrella: its alternatives are local key import, generic mnemonic validation or Base58 decoding. Its sole attack consumer retains exactly those three alternatives, and all constituent detections remain.
Removed collector-controlled archive-path-only SDK identity evidence. No current sample matched it; content/manifest identity observations remain.

Qualified the shell-backtick detector with an actual Markdown heading/fence plus documentation extension profile, defeated by an explicit shell shebang. Real Markdown fences caused the false match; valid shebang scripts with Markdown extensions retain execution coverage.
Added notable Babel AST parsing/traversal and Ed25519 signing/random private-key generation, plus actual no-window CreateProcess argument and updater-named AppData DLL path observations.
Added two hostile composites for distinct implemented outcomes, with generic behavior/disguise predicates; no hash, exact attacker peer or family token is required.
